narratives.name: Container Management Domain Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the Container Management Domain alpha matters within the three-level framework.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers evaluating container platforms face a fragmented landscape where managed Kubernetes services (EKS, AKS, GKE) offer cloud-specific convenience but lack consistent hybrid operations, while alternative distributions (Rancher) provide management layers without the integrated security, developer experience, and enterprise support of a full platform.

The Container Management TDP structures OpenShift positioning around the customer's specific container use case -- standard enterprise workloads, AI/ML workloads requiring GPU orchestration and model serving, multi-cluster governance across distributed environments, or sovereignty-aware deployments requiring data residency and regulatory compliance. Each use case maps to a dedicated tactic with audience-segmented content, competitive differentiation, and proof activity guidance.

Sellers who position OpenShift through the Container Management TDP's tactic-aligned approach establish technology-specific credibility and demonstrate understanding of the customer's container platform decision context, leading to higher win rates against both managed Kubernetes services and alternative enterprise distributions.

narratives.name: Container Management TDP Practice Intent
narratives.description: The end-to-end narrative of the container management technology domain engagement from discovery through expansion.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers evaluate container management platforms across diverse use cases -- standard Kubernetes workloads, AI/ML workloads requiring GPU orchestration, multi-cluster governance across hybrid environments, and sovereignty-aware deployments requiring data residency controls. Each scenario demands specialized positioning that connects OpenShift capabilities to customer-specific technology decisions.

The Container Management TDP validates positioning through four specialized tactics, each addressing a distinct entry point into the container platform conversation. Kubernetes Standard Workloads covers enterprise container adoption; Kubernetes for AI addresses AI platform partnership scenarios; Multicluster Security focuses on governance and policy across distributed clusters; Sovereign Infrastructure intersects with sovereignty requirements for regulated deployments.

Tactic-level engagement equips sellers with audience-segmented content (What to Say/Share/Show) for each container scenario. Competitive positioning against EKS, AKS, GKE, and Rancher is structured per tactic, with OpenShift's enterprise security, multi-cluster management through ACM, and hybrid cloud consistency as primary differentiators.

Field execution navigates between tactic-specific conversations and broader play-level value articulation. Sellers assess container adoption maturity, design platform architecture recommendations, and validate technical fit through demonstrations and proof activities tailored to the customer's container use case.

Technical validation through proof activities (POC deployments, workload compatibility testing, security compliance validation) confirms OpenShift's fit for the customer's container platform decision, leading to platform selection and subscription commitment.

Post-decision expansion identifies cross-sell opportunities across Automation and AI Platform TDPs, establishing expansion roadmaps that grow the container platform footprint from initial adoption to enterprise-wide standardization.

narratives.name: Kubernetes Standard Workloads Tactic Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the Kubernetes Standard Workloads Tactic matters for enterprise container adoption conversations.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations adopting Kubernetes for standard enterprise workloads often face a choice between managed cloud services that lock them into a single provider and self-managed distributions that require significant operational expertise without enterprise support or integrated security.

The Kubernetes Standard Workloads tactic positions OpenShift as the enterprise Kubernetes platform that combines cloud-native simplicity with enterprise-grade security, multi-cluster management, and consistent hybrid cloud operations. Conversation content is structured by audience (infrastructure leaders, platform engineers, DevOps teams) with discovery questions tailored to standard container adoption challenges.

Tactic execution establishes OpenShift's differentiation through integrated security, developer experience, and operational consistency across hybrid environments, converting container platform evaluations into qualified opportunities.

narratives.name: Multicluster Security Tactic Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the Multicluster Security Tactic matters for multi-cluster governance conversations.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations with distributed Kubernetes environments across on-premise, cloud, and edge locations face escalating governance challenges -- inconsistent security policies across clusters, compliance drift, limited observability into distributed workloads, and operational overhead from managing each cluster independently.

The Multicluster Security tactic positions OpenShift with Advanced Cluster Management as the enterprise governance layer for distributed Kubernetes. Content addresses security leaders (policy consistency, compliance automation), platform engineers (centralized management, GitOps-driven policy), and compliance officers (audit trails, regulatory reporting) with evidence of governance at enterprise scale.

Tactic execution demonstrates centralized governance value through ACM-based policy enforcement, compliance reporting, and multi-cluster observability, converting governance concerns into platform standardization opportunities across the enterprise's Kubernetes estate.

narratives.name: Sovereign Infrastructure Tactic Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the Sovereign Infrastructure Tactic matters for sovereignty-aware container deployment conversations.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations in regulated industries or sovereignty-sensitive geographies need container platforms that meet data residency requirements, provide supply chain transparency, and operate within sovereign cloud boundaries -- requirements that public cloud managed Kubernetes services may not address without significant architectural concessions.

The Sovereign Infrastructure tactic positions OpenShift as the sovereignty-aware container platform with flexible deployment models (on-premise, sovereign cloud partnerships, air-gapped environments), open-source supply chain transparency, and data residency controls. This tactic intersects with the Digital Sovereignty Sales Play for customers requiring comprehensive sovereignty strategy beyond container infrastructure.

Tactic execution establishes OpenShift's sovereignty credentials through deployment flexibility, open-source transparency, and regulatory compliance evidence, converting sovereignty requirements into differentiated container platform opportunities in regulated markets.

narratives.name: Container Management Competitive Position Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why container-domain competitive intelligence is essential for Kubernetes platform positioning.

narrativeContexts.context: Container platform evaluations increasingly involve managed Kubernetes services (EKS, AKS, GKE) that offer cloud-provider-integrated simplicity, alongside multi-cluster management tools (Rancher) that provide distribution-agnostic management. Each alternative has genuine strengths that must be acknowledged while positioning OpenShift's enterprise platform advantages.

Managed Kubernetes services excel at cloud-specific deployment simplicity and tight integration with provider services. Rancher provides multi-cluster management across distributions. However, managed services create cloud lock-in, lack consistent hybrid operations, and require bolting on enterprise security capabilities that OpenShift integrates natively.

OpenShift differentiates through integrated enterprise security (built-in rather than bolt-on), consistent hybrid cloud operations (same platform on-premise, cloud, and edge), Advanced Cluster Management for multi-cluster governance, an extensive operator ecosystem, and Red Hat's enterprise support and lifecycle management -- capabilities that address enterprise requirements managed services and alternative distributions handle through fragmented tooling.

narratives.name: Container Competitive Battle Card Context
narratives.description: Why container-domain competitive intelligence is structured as a multi-level battle card.

narrativeContexts.context: Container platform competitive intelligence must address four distinct competitive dynamics -- managed Kubernetes services from hyperscalers (EKS, AKS, GKE) competing on simplicity and cloud integration, and multi-cluster management alternatives (Rancher) competing on distribution agnosticism and management flexibility.

Each competitor class has genuine strengths. Managed services offer frictionless cloud-native deployment. Rancher provides multi-distribution management. OpenShift competes with integrated enterprise capabilities spanning security, developer experience, and operational consistency.

Battle card depth enables sellers to position credibly against each competitor class with evidence-based arguments tailored to the customer's specific evaluation context, rather than relying on generic competitive messaging.

narratives.name: Container Strategy Assessment Approach
narratives.description: How to assess customer container strategy and select appropriate tactic.

narrativeContexts.context: Container platform engagements span diverse scenarios from greenfield Kubernetes adoption to enterprise-scale multi-cluster governance, and sellers need a structured assessment approach to identify the right tactic and positioning for each customer's container maturity and use case.

Container strategy assessment evaluates the customer's container adoption maturity (greenfield, early, scaling, enterprise), identifies the primary use case (standard workloads, AI, multi-cluster governance, sovereign), and maps cluster topology requirements. This assessment determines which of the four container management tactics is most relevant and how to position OpenShift.

A completed container strategy assessment provides the foundation for tactic selection and platform architecture design, ensuring that the engagement addresses the customer's actual container platform decision context rather than defaulting to generic Kubernetes positioning.

narratives.name: Container Platform Architecture Design Approach
narratives.description: How to design OpenShift platform architecture for customer container requirements.

narrativeContexts.context: Container platform architecture must address multiple dimensions simultaneously -- deployment topology (on-premise, cloud, hybrid, edge), multi-cluster management approach, security model, developer experience, and integration with existing infrastructure -- each requiring OpenShift-specific expertise.

Architecture design translates the container strategy assessment into a concrete OpenShift deployment plan. This includes cluster topology (ACM for multi-cluster, GitOps for configuration management), security model (RBAC, network policies, supply chain security), and developer experience specifications (self-service namespaces, CI/CD integration, developer portals).

A designed container platform architecture provides the customer with a concrete vision of their OpenShift deployment, enabling tactic-level conversations grounded in architecture specifics rather than abstract capabilities.

narratives.name: Container Competitive Positioning Approach
narratives.description: How to position OpenShift competitively against Kubernetes alternatives.

narrativeContexts.context: Container platform evaluations involve multiple competitive classes -- managed Kubernetes services from hyperscalers offering cloud-native simplicity, and multi-cluster management tools offering distribution flexibility. Each requires distinct competitive positioning approaches.

EKS, AKS, and GKE provide managed Kubernetes with deep cloud provider integration. Rancher provides multi-distribution management with Kubernetes distribution flexibility. Each has genuine strengths that effective competitive positioning must acknowledge.

OpenShift differentiates through integrated enterprise security, consistent hybrid cloud operations, Advanced Cluster Management, and Red Hat's enterprise lifecycle support. Positioning is tailored to the customer's evaluation criteria and competitive scenario rather than generic competitive messaging.

narratives.name: Container Platform Validation Approach
narratives.description: How to validate OpenShift fit for customer container platform requirements.

narrativeContexts.context: Container platform decisions require technical validation beyond demonstrations -- customers need to confirm workload compatibility, security compliance, developer experience, and operational manageability in environments representative of their production requirements.

Container platform validation follows the customer's use case. For standard workloads -- workload deployment, cluster operations, developer onboarding. For AI -- GPU scheduling, model serving pipelines, AI framework compatibility. For multi-cluster -- ACM policy deployment, multi-cluster observability, compliance reporting. For sovereign -- data residency controls, supply chain transparency, air-gapped operations.

Successful container platform validation confirms OpenShift's technical fit, advances the engagement to platform decision, and generates evidence for the Container Management TDP's customer win documentation.

narratives.name: Container Platform Decision Advancement Approach
narratives.description: How to advance container platform decision to OpenShift selection.

narrativeContexts.context: Container platform decisions involve multiple stakeholders with different evaluation criteria -- infrastructure leaders evaluate operational cost, security leaders evaluate compliance, developers evaluate experience, and procurement evaluates commercial terms. Advancing the decision requires coordinating across these perspectives.

Decision advancement synthesizes technical validation results, competitive differentiation, and business value into a unified recommendation for the customer's decision process. Subscription sizing connects platform scope to commercial terms. Cross-sell identification (Automation, AI Platform TDPs) establishes the expansion roadmap.

Successful platform decision advancement results in OpenShift selection with clear deployment plan, pipeline attribution to the Container Management TDP, and identified expansion pathways that grow the engagement beyond initial container platform adoption.
